scope: Primary documentation supporting runtime/operating review; not provider or installed-host qualification

sources.title: Python3.11 subprocess.run
sources.applies: A run timeout kills/waits for the direct child; startup is not always interruptible. An encrypted cast command timeout does not establish broadcast absence or kill every descendant. Keep durable ambiguity, no resend and real systemd group qualification.
sources.limits: No new process experiment was run; installed Foundry/systemd still need exact rehearsal.

sources.title: Python3.11 os.fsync
sources.applies: Buffered file flush plus fsync supports the existing durability boundary. Atomic naming and parent-directory durability remain distinct; local hashes do not authenticate hostile replacement.
sources.limits: No filesystem/power-loss guarantee was inferred from mocked write failures.

sources.title: systemd.kill
sources.applies: Control-group kill mode terminates remaining processes in the service group; process-only mode is inadequate for signer containment. Current source uses group kill plus SIGKILL and no core dumps.
sources.limits: Current official semantics were consulted. A configured unit is not proof that an actual>=240manager applied its settings or killed descendants.

sources.title: systemd.service watchdog
sources.applies: Main-process progress notifications and an external service manager provide stall supervision; a timer thread could mask blocked work. Keep health/readiness/freshness and watchdog meanings separate.
sources.limits: No systemd install/restart/monitor action was performed.

sources.title: Python3.11 exclusive open
sources.applies: Exclusive creation distinguishes reservation from a late existence check. New verification files must be owned before selected module imports/test bodies or source scans.
sources.limits: Actual Windows restrictions caused two explicit filesystem-case skips; no Linux execution is inferred.

sources.title: Linux open(2) file descriptors and O_EXCL
sources.applies: O_CREAT|O_EXCL rejects existing targets; writes through an already-owned descriptor remain attached to its open file description rather than a replacement pathname. Final identity checks also reject replaced pathnames.
sources.limits: Not authentication against a hostile filesystem owner or a blanket power-loss/network-filesystem guarantee; real supported-host qualification remains open.

conclusion: The established controlled rollout/reconciliation model remains appropriate; the new fixes close concrete continuity/evidence gaps without changing financial policy.
